extracted.intended_audience: federal technology and policy professionals, policymakers, and the interested public
extracted.subtask_description: Recommendations and standards for securing and improving government public-comment systems to prevent fraudulent/automated submissions, increase transparency, and hold bad actors accountable. Focuses on technical, legal, and procedural reforms agencies and lawmakers should adopt.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institute CAPTCHA security tests
rubrics_metrics.description: The report calls for the institution of CAPTCHA security tests at a minimum on agencies' comment submission systems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CAPTCHA tests are a baseline measure to prevent simple automated submissions, but the report cautions they will not be sufficient alone.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monitor and mitigate automated traffic
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies should find and implement strategies for monitoring and mitigating automated traffic to comment systems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Beyond CAPTCHA, technical strategies and ongoing monitoring are needed to detect and limit bot-driven or automated mass submissions that distort rulemaking inputs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Require intermediary disclosure with each submitted comment
rubrics_metrics.description: Intermediaries (such as lead generators or third-party services) should be required, with each comment submitted, to disclose the intermediary's identity and the identities of any parties that assisted in generating or submitting the comment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This increases transparency about who actually authored or assisted in producing comments and helps distinguish genuine public input from orchestrated campaigns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Punish organizations that submit fake comments
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies should punish advocacy organizations found to have submitted fake or fabricated comments in rulemaking proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enforcement can include civil penalties, disgorgements, and other agency-level sanctions; the report cites settlements that included monetary penalties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strengthen impersonation and anti-deception laws
rubrics_metrics.description: Lawmakers should strengthen impersonation laws and explicitly prohibit deceptive and unauthorized comments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statutory changes would provide criminal or civil tools to deter and prosecute impersonation and deceptive practices used to manufacture the appearance of public support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hold corporations and executives criminally or administratively accountable
rubrics_metrics.description: The report and commentators call for holding companies, executives, and potentially public officials accountable for orchestrating or funding fraudulent comment campaigns, including pursuing criminal charges where appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommendations include investigations into executives' conduct, potential firings, and legislative fixes if existing laws are insufficient.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibit astroturfing and require transparency about paid/orchestrated campaigns
rubrics_metrics.description: Disguising orchestrated, paid campaigns as grassroots public support (astroturfing) is unacceptable and should be prohibited or transparently disclosed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The report labels disguised paid campaigns as astroturfing and recommends measures to prevent creating a false appearance of genuine, unpaid public support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulate lead generators and ban fabrication of consumer responses
rubrics_metrics.description: Lead generators (commercial firms hired to recruit commenters) must not fabricate consumer responses or use deceptive incentives to create mass comments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The report documents lead generators using prizes and sweepstakes to lure consumers but then fabricating responses; policies should ban such deceptive tactics and require verification of recruited participants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technical modernization and capacity improvements for comment systems
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies should make technical changes to clean up the comment-making process, including ensuring comment systems can handle large volumes of legitimate traffic and are resilient to outages or abuse.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Past incidents (e.g., system failures during mass commenting events) highlighted the need for improved infrastructure and security practices to accurately capture public input.
